title: Your Personalized Results
intro: Based on what you've shared about your preferences, here's how each PrEP option lines up with what matters most to you. Remember - all three options are highly effective. The best one is the one you'll use consistently.

oral.name: Daily Pill (tenofovir/emtricitabine)
oral.heading: Oral PrEP might be a great fit for you
reasons: You can take it at home on your own schedule - no clinic visits for each dose
It's easy to start and easy to stop whenever your needs change
It has the longest track record of safe use
Generic versions are available, which may lower your cost
considerations: You'll need to remember to take a pill every day for full protection
Having pills at home means others might see them
You'll need lab work and check-ins every 3 months
Mild start-up side effects like nausea are possible but usually pass quickly
providerQuestions: Which oral PrEP medication - Truvada or Descovy - would you recommend for me?
Are there any reasons one oral PrEP option might be better for my health than the other?
What should I do if I miss a dose?
How often will I need to come in for check-ups and lab work?
Are there programs to help me pay for oral PrEP?

on_demand.name: On-Demand Pill (tenofovir/emtricitabine 2-1-1)
on_demand.heading: On-demand PrEP might be a great fit for you
reasons: You only take pills when you need them, not every day
You take it at home on your own schedule with no injections needed
Uses less medication overall, which may lower costs
Easy to start and stop whenever your needs change
Studied and shown to be highly effective when used correctly
considerations: You need to plan ahead and take the first dose at least 2 hours before sex
Currently recommended only for cisgender men who have sex with men
Requires following the 2-1-1 schedule carefully for full protection
Daily PrEP may be a better fit if you have sex very frequently
Only studied with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (Truvada), not tenofovir alafenamide (Descovy)
providerQuestions: Is on-demand (2-1-1) PrEP a good option for my situation?
How do I make sure I'm following the dosing schedule correctly?
What should I do if I forget to take the before-sex dose?
Should I consider switching to daily PrEP if my situation changes?
Are there programs to help me pay for tenofovir/emtricitabine?

injectable_2mo.name: 2-Month Injection (cabotegravir)
injectable_2mo.heading: The every-2-month injection might be a great fit for you
reasons: No daily pill to remember - your protection is built in at each appointment
Clinical studies showed it was even more effective than daily pills
More private - no medication to keep at home
You only need to think about your PrEP every 2 months
considerations: You'll start with a month of daily pills to make sure you tolerate the medication
Requires a clinic visit every 2 months for the injection
You'll get a shot in the buttock, which may cause temporary soreness
If you stop, the medicine stays in your body for 12+ months - you'll need a plan for continued protection during that time
Not all clinics offer this option yet
providerQuestions: Do you offer the cabotegravir (Apretude) injection at this clinic?
What should I expect during the oral lead-in period?
What happens if I'm late for an injection appointment?
If I decide to stop, what's the plan for staying protected during the tail period?
How is the injection given, and how long does the appointment take?

injectable_6mo.name: 6-Month Injection (lenacapavir)
injectable_6mo.heading: The twice-yearly injection might be a great fit for you
reasons: Only two clinic visits per year - the most convenient dosing schedule available
No daily pills to remember between appointments
Highly effective - 96% reduction in HIV risk in clinical trials
Very private - no medication at home after the initial loading phase
Minimal time spent thinking about HIV prevention
considerations: It's a newer option and may not be available at all clinics yet
Some medications and supplements (like St. John's wort) can interact with it - tell your provider about everything you take
You'll get a small injection under the skin in the belly area
If you stop, the medicine stays in your body for an extended period - work with your provider on a transition plan
Insurance coverage may vary since it's a newer medication
providerQuestions: Do you offer lenacapavir (Yeztugo) for PrEP at this clinic?
Will any of my current medications or supplements interact with lenacapavir?
What does the oral loading phase involve?
If I decide to stop, how do we plan for continued protection?
What are my options if my insurance doesn't cover this yet?

providerSection.heading: Ways to Start the Conversation with Your Provider
providerSection.intro: Talking to your provider about PrEP doesn't have to be complicated. Here are some conversation starters you can use:
tips: "I've been learning about PrEP and I'm interested in starting. Can we talk about which option might be right for me?"
"I'd like to know more about the different ways to take PrEP - the daily pill, the 2-month shot, and the 6-month shot."
"I've been thinking about HIV prevention and I'd like to explore PrEP. What would the next steps be?"
"I used a decision tool that helped me think about my PrEP options. Can I share what I learned with you?"
"I have some questions about PrEP side effects and what to expect. Can we go through them together?"
